##Code


```{r}
analyze_drug_binding <- function(pdb_id) {

  pdb <- read.pdb(pdb_id)
  pdb_chainA <- trim.pdb(pdb, chain = "A", elety = "CA")
  b_factors <- pdb_chainA$atom$b

  plotb3(b_factors,
         sse = pdb_chainA,
         typ = "l",
         ylab = "B-factor",
         main = paste("B-factor plot for", pdb_id))

  return(b_factors)
}

b1 <- analyze_drug_binding("4AKE")
b2 <- analyze_drug_binding("1AKE")
b3 <- analyze_drug_binding("1E4Y")

```


> Q. Comments on what are the inputs to the function

The inputs the functions is pdb_id. This input is a character string that tells the function which protein structure to load an analyze. 

> Q. what the function does and how to use it.

The function reads a protein structure from the PDB, extracts only chain A and the C-alpha atoms, pulls out their B-factors, and make a line plot showing the B-factor pattern for that protein. You use the function by giving it a PDB ID as a character string. The function will automatically download teh structure, process it, and show the B-factor plot. 

> Q. what is the output of the function.

The output of the function is a numeric vector of B-factors for chain A C-alpha atoms from the protein you selected.
